newsitem.title: BELGIUM: E.Zaireans in Belgium call for end to border war.
newsitem.headline: E.Zaireans in Belgium call for end to border war.

text.p: A group of Zairean nationals from the eastern region of Kivu on Tuesday called for an end to the conflict along the Zaire-Rwanda border that has left more than a million refugees facing starvation and death.

"Thousands of Zairean and Rwandan men, women and children are dying today amid general indifference. This war is not our war. Let's end it with a frank and sustained dialogue," Jean- Pierre Muongo of the Sima-Kivu group told a news conference.

Registered in Belgium as a non-profit body, Sima-Kivu says it is an apolitical association concerned with the socio-cultural issues in Kivu and supporting the people there through non-governmental organisations and local contacts.

Recent fighting between the Zairean army and Tutsi-led rebels in the Kivu region has left 1.2 million Hutu refugees with scant food and water. The United Nations reported on Sunday that thousands were dying each hour.
Muongo added that the people of central Africa must seek greater unity. No single African state had the forces necessary to protect the borders they inherited from European occupation, he said.

The group's president Emmanuel Nashi said continuation of the war would amount to "collective suicide" by the populations involved. "If we don't end the war immediately, the war will put an end to our countries and our peoples. No one will come out a winner..."
Nashi also questioned the length of time the international community had taken to respond to the crises.

"It's almost two months since Zaire was subjected to outside aggression from Rwanda with its allies...We wonder about the heavy silence from governments of free and democratic states faced with such a flagrant violation of international law," he added.
